Sanguine-Monsters-Chronos.notes: The manual describes a Chronos context menu for choosing which polyphonic channel each section's light shows. The installed build has no such menu: chronos.cpp overrides no appendContextMenu, and the string "LEDs channel" appears in the binary only for Fortuna. The ledsChannel value exists in the Chronos code and stays at channel 1. The wave outputs have no single voltage range: they span 0V to 10V with bipolar mode off and ±5V with it on, so no range is recorded for them.

lines: Two polyphonic coin tossers, each sending its input signal to one of two outputs on every trigger, with a crossfade so the swap does not click
Sets the odds of the toss for that section: at the top every trigger sends the signal to A, at the bottom every trigger sends it to B in direct mode or swaps the outputs in toggle mode
Chooses how the toss is read, the panel printing M: Direct sends the signal to A on heads and to B on tails; Toggle leaves it where it is on heads and swaps it over on tails. It comes up in Direct
Sets how long the signal takes to fade from one output to the other after a swap, 0 to 10 seconds; at 0 the crossfader is off and the swap is instant
The signal that section routes to one of its two outputs; the second section's is normalled to the first section's
Shifts the odds for that section; the voltage is divided by 5 and added to the probability slider, and it is read one voltage per channel
A trigger above 2V tosses the coin for that section and chooses an output; the second section's is normalled to the first section's
One of the two destinations for that section's signal; it carries the input while it is selected and silence while it is not, with the crossfade between
Note — Polyphony for a section comes from its signal and trigger inputs, whichever carries more channels; a monophonic probability CV modulates channel 1 only.
Note — The second section's trigger input is normalled to the first section's, so one trigger can drive both halves; the manual mentions only the signal normalling.
Note — A signal is always at one output or the other: a new module, or a freshly loaded patch, sends it to A.
Menu — LEDs channel — picks which polyphonic channel the lights on both sections show; only channels the cables carry are listed, and it defaults to channel 1

lines: An expander that selects any step of a Gegenees or a Hydra directly, one trigger input per step; a Gegenees goes immediately to its left and a Hydra immediately to its right
A trigger here selects that step on the connected switch; where two arrive at once the higher numbered step wins
Note — The expander does nothing on its own: it has to be placed beside a Gegenees or a Hydra, and it can serve one of each at the same time, driving both.
Note — The arrow lights show which steps are available: they follow the Steps knob of the connected switch, pointing left for a Gegenees and right for a Hydra.

lines: An expander for Alchemist, going immediately to its left, that adds mute-all and solo-all buttons, an exclusive mode for each, and polyphonic CV over every channel's mute and solo
Mutes and unmutes all sixteen Alchemist channels at once; it is switched off again by a solo-all, or by unmuting or soloing any single channel on the Alchemist
Makes muting one channel on the Alchemist unmute all the others; the panel prints EX., and turning it on takes the mute-all button out of use
Solos and unsolos all sixteen Alchemist channels at once; it is switched off again by a mute-all, or by unsoloing or muting any single channel on the Alchemist

Engages mute-all while the voltage stands at 1V or more

Engages solo-all while the voltage stands at 1V or more
Solos each Alchemist channel whose voltage on this polyphonic cable stands at 1V or more, one channel of cable per mixer channel
